intuition.title: Reducing cadmium precursor reactivity for CdTe
intuition.text: Cadmium myristate with tellurium powder is described as insufficiently reactive, whereas cadmium myristate with tributylphosphine telluride is too reactive. The authors instead form a less reactive cadmium octadecylphosphonate precursor. These failed alternatives lack complete experimental details and are retained as qualitative comparisons rather than invented recipes.

intuition.title: Potential scale-up is an outlook
intuition.text: Heating a mixture without rapid precursor injection could simplify process control and scaling, according to the authors. The article does not demonstrate an industrial production run, a scale-up yield, or a validated manufacturing cost.

general_background.title: Octadecene is not always inert
general_background.summary: Octadecene provides a weakly coordinating medium for hot solution growth, leaving the ligands more freedom to control surface binding. It can also polymerize under growth conditions, leaving an alkene-derived residue that is difficult to separate from hydrophobic nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Cadmium oxide needs conversion to a soluble feed
general_background.summary: Cadmium oxide is a solid precursor that can be converted into a soluble cadmium complex by an acidic ligand. That conversion makes it possible to control the cadmium delivered during nucleation without using a volatile organocadmium feed.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Formation of High-Quality CdTe, CdSe, and CdS Nanocrystals Using CdO as Precursor

general_background.title: Tributylphosphine as a chalcogen carrier
general_background.summary: Tributylphosphine can react with elemental chalcogen to form a soluble molecular phosphine chalcogenide feed. When that feed supplies growing nanocrystals, its conversion rate affects the availability of chalcogen for nucleation and growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Molecular Control of the Nanoscale: Effect of Phosphine–Chalcogenide Reactivity on CdS–CdSe Nanocrystal Composition and Morphology

general_background.title: Excluding air during colloidal growth
general_background.summary: An argon atmosphere can limit contact between air and reactive precursors during hot colloidal growth. Protecting the feed from oxidation helps keep the supply of growth species distinct from side reactions with air.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
